entities.name: PMID:25425321
observations: BMC Cardiovascular Disorders (2014) study of 739 middle-aged Finnish patients with type 2 diabetes without prior major cardiovascular events, followed for 18 years.
Prolonged P-wave duration was defined as ≥114 ms; prevalent non-major macrovascular disease included ischemic ECG changes with typical angina or claudication.

Among patients with prevalent non-major macrovascular disease, prolonged P-wave duration was associated with 2.45-fold higher stroke mortality (95% CI 1.11–5.37). No relationship was observed in patients without prevalent non-major macrovascular disease.
The study used Cox proportional-hazards modeling and assessed stroke mortality; the finding supports prediction within the specified subgroup but is observational and based on 59 stroke deaths.

entities.name: P-wave stroke mortality
observations: In type 2 diabetic patients with prevalent non-major macrovascular disease, prolonged P-wave duration (≥114 ms) predicted stroke mortality over 18 years: hazard estimate 2.45, 95% CI 1.11–5.37.
The association was not present among type 2 diabetic patients without prevalent non-major macrovascular disease.
